title: sse: fix streaming chunking/framing edge cases (partial JSON, delimiters, ordering)
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fixes several SSE streaming edge cases that could result in partial/invalid JSON being emitted, incorrect token/event ordering across chunk boundaries, and missing/duplicate delimiters. Improves stability for OpenAI-compat streaming adapters and reduces sporadic downstream parser errors.
description:
Context and motivation:
Users (and our OpenAI-compat adapter) have sporadically observed malformed streaming events: partial JSON objects when tokens split across chunks, missing or duplicate 'data:' delimiters when the framer boundary falls inside a token, and rare reordering between token events when multiple streaming pipelines race. These manifest as downstream JSON parse errors, duplicated events in the client, or slightly out-of-order tokens that break structured output and function-calling heuristics.

What this PR changes (single-line summary):
Improve the SSE framer and chunking logic to buffer partial JSON tokens, emit well-formed event boundaries, and add lightweight ordering metadata to prevent interleaving races. Update OpenAI-compat streaming adapter to tolerate the improved framing and add regression tests.

Detailed notes (what/why/how):
- Buffer-aware framer: the framer now maintains a small append-only buffer when a chunk ends with an incomplete JSON token (e.g. inside a string or unfinished object). We attempt to detect valid JSON boundaries using a combination of delimiter scanning and a cheap bracket/string state machine rather than a full JSON parser to keep latency low.
- Delimiter handling: unify how 'data: ' and '\n' delimiters are emitted. Previously a trailing token that ended exactly at a chunk boundary could cause the next chunk to emit an extra 'data:' header. The framer now ensures a single header per logical event and trims accidental duplicates.
- Partial JSON reassembly: when the framer detects a likely partial JSON payload, it holds emission until the next chunk provides a closing boundary (with a short timeout fallback to avoid head-of-line blocking for very sparse producers). This eliminates the common partial-JSON parse errors seen in logs.
- Ordering protection: for the small number of cases where the concurrency between tokenizer->streamer and streamer->adapter pipelines caused observable reordering, we attach a lightweight monotonically increasing event_seq header in the SSE meta block (internal-only, not exposed in public payloads). Consumers ignore it, but our OpenAI-compat adapter uses it to reorder buffered events if necessary. This prevents token interleaving without changing public semantics.
- OpenAI-compat adapter: updated to accept the new framing (single-header enforcement and soft ordering header), and to transparently drop the internal event_seq meta when presenting events to the public API. Also tightened the parser to be tolerant to small whitespace differences.
- Testing: added unit tests for the framer state machine, integration tests that simulate chunk splits inside strings/objects, and a stress test that reproduces the previous interleaving race. All tests included.
- Performance: microbenchmarked to ensure median latency impact is <0.5ms per event at 99th percentile for typical payload sizes; batching behavior unchanged.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for framer state transitions
- [x] Integration tests simulating partial JSON chunks
- [x] Update OpenAI-compat adapter parsing logic
- [x] Benchmarked for latency/regression
- [x] Added changelog/release notes

Backports: This is low-risk but affects runtimes; request backport to v1.18.x for on-prem customers (label 'backport' added).

Notes on CI: initial run failed a flaky stress-test (race in the stress harness); I made a small harness fix and re-ran — green on final.

Related: ENG-6321 (streaming parsers), ENG-6387 (sse perf flakiness), SUP-4492 customer report about malformed streaming JSON.

review_comments: Priya Reddy: Found one edge case where a chunk boundary splits a multibyte UTF-8 sequence; please ensure buffer scanning handles byte boundaries. Also left a small nit on a variable name.
Maya Chen: Good catch — updated framer to scan at byte granularity and added UTF-8 split test in the integration suite.
Chen Wu: Would prefer a shorter timeout for buffer flush in low-throughput streams (reduce head-of-line blocking). Can we make it configurable per route?
Maya Chen: Made timeout configurable via stream config with 50ms default; documented in streaming.md. This should be safe for most real workloads.
Liam O'Connor: Verified the stress harness reproduces the prior race and confirms the fix. Approving.
